findings: CONTENT SLOT VALUE MODEL. The only thing a content run hands the site is `slot-values.json`, a bare `{ slotKey: SlotValue }` map (SlotValue = string | {src,alt?,srcset?}). `buildOverlayValues` (overlay.ts) copies `result.slotValues` verbatim — no filtering, no envelope — because production/run.ts:234,375, seo/production-plan.ts and the freshness hash all read it as a bare map. Any richer per-slot record MUST be a sibling file; `slot-accounting.json` is the established precedent (accounting.ts writes it beside, never into, the overlay). `effectiveSlotValues` = template defaults overlaid by the run; `changedKeys` = keys whose JSON differs from the default.

AUTHORED.SLOTVALUES APPLICATION PATH (the authoritative one). release/instance.ts `resolutionSlotValues()` collects ONLY `routeContent[*].slotValues` + `urls` from a pack; `foldResolutionIntoAuthored()` merges those into `project.authored.slotValues` (later packs win). At build, `contentStageRunner` (stages.ts:69-210) prepares a BRAND-NEW content run, merges base `generation-result.json` slotValues, then routeContent, then urls, then `authored.slotValues` LAST — every one of those stamped `sources[key]="user-provided"` and removed from `unresolved` — and calls `ingestGenerationResult`, which MATERIALIZES a fresh `slot-values.json`. The doctrine is stated identically in three places on purpose: release/store.ts:19-29, release/resolve.ts:180-186, and content-injection/run.ts:271-276 (`CONTENT_WRITE_DOCTRINE_WARNING`), surfaced to operators only by cli-content-validate.ts:40 when `manifest.manualEdits` is true.

SLOT ACCOUNTING — TWO ORTHOGONAL AXES, exact enum values. ORIGIN (`SLOT_ORIGINS`, 5): `user-provided`, `derived-copy`, `generated-marketing`, `synthetic-fact`, `source-preserved`. DISPOSITION (`SLOT_DISPOSITIONS`, 5): `applied`, `preserved`, `removed`, `human-required`, `unresolved`. Each in-scope slot carries EXACTLY ONE of each plus `customerFacing: confirmed|ambiguous` (confirmed == compiler said editability="editable"; ambiguous == review-flagged, never folded into a success number). `reconciliation` proves it inside the artifact: uniqueSlotKeys == inScopeSlots, originTotal == dispositionTotal == inScopeSlots, with `missing[]`/`doubleCounted[]` names. The in-scope population is `inScopeSlotKeys()` = every unit slot + every `reviewSlotKeys` entry. `scopeHonesty.templateExcludedCandidates` records the candidates the template compiler suppressed before slotting — they never reach the account at all.

FACT TRUTH MODES. `CONTENT_TRUTH_MODES = ["verified-only", "synthetic-allowed"]`, default `verified-only` (DEFAULT_CONTENT_TRUTH_MODE). Enforcement is an ENGINE step, not a prompt: `applyTruthMode` runs FIRST inside `ingestGenerationResult` (run.ts:224-229), before validation and before any overlay exists. Seven deterministic claim regexes over produced text/url values: counted-metric, price, percentage, phone-number, certification-or-award, superlative-social-proof, founding-date; plus `declared-synthetic` when the generator self-declares. Exemptions in order: sources[key]==="user-provided"; claim text contained in a `providedFacts` entry; value normalizes equal to the template default (that is source carry-over, brand-leak's axis). Otherwise verified-only REFUSES (key leaves slotValues, enters `unresolved` with reason `needs factual input: unsupported <claim> claim (content truth mode: verified-only)`) and synthetic-allowed KEEPS + marks `synthetic-fact`. Decisions recorded as `{slotKey, claim, decision: refused-unresolved|marked-synthetic|backed-by-user-fact, detail}` in `slot-accounting.json.truthDecisions`. `nextResult.synthetic` is always REWRITTEN, never inherited.

BATCHING. `BATCH_UNIT_LIMIT = 40` (packet.ts:53). `buildBatches` cuts global units first, then per-route chunks; ids are assigned ONCE at prepare time and persisted in `generation-request.json`. `executeGenerationBatches` consumes those persisted batches (never re-plans), issues one `generate()` per batch with `narrowRequest` (the same packet narrowed to one batch), and records a `BatchCallRecord` + a telemetry event per call. `mergeBatchResults` enforces three rules with NO last-write-wins: a key may only come from the batch owning its unit (`out-of-batch-key`), may only be produced once (`duplicate-slot-value`/`duplicate-unresolved`/`duplicate-image-brief`), and may not be assigned by one batch while another marks it needs-input (`assigned-and-unresolved-across-batches`). First writer's value is kept for determinism, the conflict is recorded, and `assertNoBatchConflicts` throws so the caller FAILS the run. Site plan identity comes from `entries[0]`; page plans merge by route, first writer wins.

GED-D GUARD. `MAX_REPAIR_ITERATIONS = 2`. `RepairProgressGuard.evaluate` is stateful across one loop and checks in specificity order: (1) `no-candidate-keys-changed` — the repair produced nothing different from the current overlay; (2) `repair-values-identical` — byte-identical to the previous iteration's values; (3) `failure-signature-repeated` — same `failureSignatureOf()` (sha256-16 over sorted repairCandidates `slotKey|reason|evidence` plus failing `route@width|notes`) AND the same candidate set. `REPAIR_STOP_REASONS` (7): `layout-qa-passed`, `no-repair-candidates`, `iteration-bound-reached`, `repair-values-identical`, `failure-signature-repeated`, `no-candidate-keys-changed`, `repair-validation-failed`. Stops persist to `report/repair/repair-stop.json` and to `manifest.repairStop`. `buildRepairRequest` deliberately SKIPS `unslotted-duplicate-text-desync` and `stale-duplicate-text-remnant` candidates — those are operator decisions, not rewritable sentences. Only the guard half of GED-D shipped; the provider half (`fakeText` length-awareness) is out of scope because smoke:seo/release/production all pin its literal output.

TELEMETRY. `src/telemetry/` is provider-neutral and OPTIONAL everywhere — no recorder means no file and identical pipeline behaviour. `generation-telemetry-v1`, append-only JSONL at `report/telemetry.jsonl` (cli-content-generate.ts:81-82, cli-content-qa.ts:164-165). Event fields: engine, runId, seamId (`content.generate.batch`), stage (`initial`|`repair`|`manual`), callIndex, provider, model?, batchIds, unitCount, slotCount, routes, elapsedMs, retryCount, outcome (`ok`|`error`), error?, usage?. `usage` is OMITTED ENTIRELY unless the provider reported it (`generator.lastUsage?.()`) — never zero-filled, never estimated. The manual `--result <file>` seam therefore leaves it absent, which is the correct record.

BRANDLEAKWARNING KIND ENUM (types.ts:503-517), exactly 5: `brand-token-in-value`, `brand-token-in-untouched-default`, `original-external-url-retained`, `original-external-url-in-untouched-default`, `blocked-visible-source-content`. `severity` is optional (`warning`|`blocker`); only `blocked-visible-source-content` is emitted at blocker severity, and only when the slot key appears in `engineBlockedKeys` — derived in run.ts:150-154 from unresolved entries whose reason contains `ENGINE_LIMITATION_MARKER` ("engine-limitation"). Detection is deterministic MVP: `brandTokensFromHost(host)` word-boundary matching, plus external URL slots whose effective value still equals the source default. A separate, wider surface vocabulary lives in brand-surfaces.ts (`BRAND_SURFACES`, 14 values) and feeds the release layer's `brand-leak` requirement kind — it is DETECTOR ONLY, with neutralization explicitly deferred to bake.

PRODUCTION BAKE SHAPE. `production-spec-v1` (production/types.ts) pins template/contentRun/theme/seoPlan/assets each by `{dir, hash(dir-sha256-v1), fileCount, byteCount, excluded}` plus per-layer ids, written BEFORE the bake so the build is reproducible from named, verified inputs. Outputs go to two additive namespaces: `data/<host>/production-specs/<run-id>/production-spec.json` and `data/<host>/production-builds/<run-id>/{app/, package/, report/bake-report.json, manifest.json (production-build-v1)}`. `BakeReport` is the per-layer accounting (content/theme/seo/assets/build); `DeployManifest` (`production-deploy-manifest-v1`) is what QA reads so it never touches a run directory. `buildMode.chosen` enum has `standalone-server` but `runProductionCompile` always writes `static-export`, and `convertToStaticExport` THROWS if the route table carries any query-variant key.

BAKE STEPS A–F. A content: overlay → `app/template-data/slot-values.baked.json` + `patchSlotContent` removes the `WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE` env seam. B theme: overlay css → `app/public/wr/theme-overlay.css` + `patchLayout` adds `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/wr/theme-overlay.css" precedence="wr-generated">` immediately AFTER the generated sheet (same precedence group, React preserves in-group order — byte-equivalent to the proxy's append). C seo: `bakeRouteTitles` writes plan titles into `reconstruction-data/route-map.json` so head `<title>` AND the RSC flight payload both derive from the route table (no string splicing), then `postProcessExport` splices `headHtml` before `</head>` per route, verifies `<title>escaped</title>`, and writes `robots.txt`. D assets: `copyMedia` into `out/media/`, then `applyRewrite` over every exported `.html` (html context), `.txt` RSC flight (html context) and `.css` (css context) — the Task 22 proxy's exact mechanism at build time. E/F: `assemblePackage` renames `out/` to `package/site/` and emits `server.mjs`, `deploy-manifest.json`, `RUN.md`, plus `sitemap.preview.xml` in preview only. All four source patches (patch.ts) use `requireOnce`/`requireAbsent` anchors and fail LOUDLY on a future generator's drift.

PREVIEW-VS-PRODUCTION AND THE NOINDEX RULE. Mode is inherited, never re-decided: `seoPlan.domainState.mode`, which is `preview` iff `productionDomain === undefined` (production-plan.ts:162). Preview: every route gets `robotsMeta = noindex,nofollow` in the rendered head; `canonical.finalized=false, value=null`; `og:url`/`og:image`/`twitter:site` needs-input; `robots.txt` = `User-agent: *\nDisallow: /` with NO Sitemap line (a Sitemap line needs an absolute URL and domains are never invented); `/sitemap.xml` is intentionally absent → 404 from the static host, while `sitemap.preview.xml` (path-only `<loc>`, an XML comment marking it non-conformant) ships as a package artifact only. Production: `index,follow`, self-referential canonical `https://<domain><path>`, absolute og:url, `robots.txt` Allow + `Sitemap:` line, and run.ts:387-390 COPIES the real `sitemap.xml` into `out/`. `indexabilityGate.decision` is `preview`|`indexable`; preview carries 7 machine-readable blockers from `buildPreviewBlockers` (production-domain-needs-input, seo-needs-input-values, replacement-required-assets, fonts-license-needs-review, business-facts-needs-input, uninjected-route-content, source-brand-inline-svg) — every number/name derived per site from the artifacts the evidence strings cite, and `uninjected-route-content` is DROPPED when it would read "0 of N". production/qa.ts re-asserts all of it over real HTTP: `robots-meta:<route>`, `robots-txt`, `robots-txt-no-sitemap-line`, `sitemap-preview-404`.

ASSET PIPELINE. Namespaces: `data/<host>/asset-inventories/<run-id>/` (asset-inventory.json, classification.json, font-inventory.json, manifest.json) and `data/<host>/asset-materializations/<run-id>/` (manifest.json, rewrite-map.json, replacement-manifest.json, media/, report/{network-qa.json, font-qa.json, residual-source-assets.json, derivation.json}). Inventory is built from STORED artifacts only — SiteSpec asset-catalog, `url()` in the generated stylesheet, rendered.html head favicons/og-images/font-preloads, template image-slot join, Task 19 imageBriefs — with `--live-font-css` the single bounded opt-in network access. `AssetClassification` (4): `safe-to-materialize`, `replacement-recommended`, `replacement-required`, `license-needs-review`. `MATERIALIZED_CLASSES` = the first two only; `replacement-required` and `license-needs-review` are NEVER auto-fetched (recorded `skipped-<classification>`), truncated URLs are `skipped-truncated`, and the fetch host allowlist is EXACTLY the hosts the inventory observed. Storage is `media/<sha256>.<ext>` with byte-identical dedup; the rewrite map is sorted longest-sourceUrl-first so a short URL can never steal a long one's occurrences. `residual-report.ts` (GED-G) joins the per-route runtime census with inventory identity and the replacement manifest per FILE, keeping the query string (CDN transform params identify a distinct delivered file) and stripping only the fragment; `replacement-manifest.json` remains the authority on WHETHER an asset must be replaced, the residual report only says WHERE and HOW OFTEN.

ASSETS STAGE RUNNER. `assetsStageRunner` (stages.ts:305-320) is a thin conductor over `applyAssetResolutions` (release/resolve-assets.ts). It NEVER re-runs inventory and NEVER re-fetches. It `cp`s the whole base materialization run into a new run dir (refusing if the dir exists), content-hashes each operator file into `media/<sha256><ext>`, flips the matching `replacement-manifest.json` entry to `{status:"provided", providedFile, providedBy: "release:<projectId>:<releaseRunId>"}`, updates-or-appends the rewrite-map entry for that `sourceUrl`, appends an `operator-provided` manifest entry, writes `font-decisions.json`, and recomputes `counts.uniqueFiles`/`rewriteEntries`. Crucially it INHERITS `report/network-qa.json` and `report/font-qa.json` from the base run and says so in `report/derivation.json` ("conservative: replacements only shrink the residual set; re-run assets:qa against this run to re-measure").

WHAT MAKES THE ASSETS STAGE STALE VS REUSED. `STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.assets = ["template"]` — assets does NOT depend on content, so a content edit cannot stale it. Its inputsHash (freshness.ts `computeStageInputsHash`) = sha256 over `{stage:"assets", upstream:{template:<dir hash>}, resolution:{assets: <assetId→file content sha256>, fontDecisions: <map>}}`. So assets goes stale on exactly four things: (a) the template artifact hash moves (frozen root — should never happen, and if it does `release:build` REFUSES it as frozen-stage drift); (b) `resolutionAssetContentHashes` changes — a new/removed assetId, or DIFFERENT BYTES AT THE SAME PATH (files are content-hashed, so swapping bytes in place is a change), or a file that vanished (recorded as the sentinel `missing:<file>` plus a warning); (c) `resolution.fontDecisions` changes; (d) the assets artifact directory's own bytes drift from the recorded hash. Otherwise it is REUSED verbatim. `RESOLUTION_FIELD_IMPACTS` maps both `assets` and `fontDecisions` to `["assets", "production"]`, and `downstreamOf("assets")` is exactly `["production"]` — no other stage sits below it.

WHAT AN AUTHORED ASSET REPLACEMENT WOULD HAVE TO LOOK LIKE TO STALE ONLY ASSETS. A `production-resolution-v1` pack whose ONLY populated fields are `assets` (and optionally `fontDecisions`) — no `urls`, no `routeContent`, no `facts`, no `productionBaseUrl`, no `theme`, since `fieldPresent()` in graph.ts treats any non-empty record as present and each of those pulls in content/seo/theme. Shape: `assets: { "<assetId>": "path/to/file.png" }` or `{ file, note? }`. `<assetId>` must be either an `inventoryId` that exists in the base run's `replacement-manifest.json` entries, or one of the two site-level ids `og-image` / `organization-logo` — anything else throws `resolution assets reference unknown inventory ids`. The extension must be in `EXTENSION_BY_SUFFIX` (.png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif .svg .ico .avif) and the file must exist at resolve time AND at every later `refreshStageStatuses`, because the freshness hash is taken from the ORIGINAL PATH, not from the copy inside the derived run. Result: `invalidatedStages` returns `["assets", "production"]`; content, theme and seo stay fresh and are reused; `release:build` runs `assetsStageRunner` then `productionStageRunner` and nothing else.

SEO PLAN/PREVIEW/QA. `createProductionSeoPlanRun` writes six files into `data/<host>/production-seo-plans/<run-id>/`: `production-seo-plan.json`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`|`sitemap.preview.xml`, `rendered-head.json`, `report/needs-input.json`, `manifest.json`. Every value is a `PlannedValue {status: known|needs-input, value, basis, previewFallback}` and `renderRouteHead` emits NO TAG for a needs-input value with no fallback — a missing tag is honest, an invented one is not. The only source of production copy is the content run (`sitePlan.siteIdentity` + `pagePlans`); the source snapshot is consumed for forbidden-copy comparison ONLY, and the run THROWS if `checkForbiddenCopy` or `checkBrandIsolation` fails. Preview serving (`seo/serve.ts` `rewriteHtmlHead`) does three ordered things: substitute every encoded occurrence of the upstream title (so the RSC flight payload cannot revert the tab title at hydration), rewrite the `<title>` element with `escapeForTitleText`, then splice `headHtml` before `</head>` between the `wr-seo-head-start`/`wr-seo-head-end` markers. `escape-variants.ts` (GED-E) supplies six encodings — `raw`, `html-hex-apostrophe`, `html-decimal-apostrophe`, `html-named-apostrophe`, `json`, `json-html-escaped` — sorted longest-needle-first, with the REPLACEMENT carried in the SAME encoding as the occurrence (so a raw context gets raw bytes and an HTML context gets `&`, never `&amp;`), applied by literal split/join, never a regex over page bytes. The production bake reproduces the identical result by baking titles into `route-map.json` rather than substituting, and `escapeForTitleText` is deliberately the same escape set as bake.ts's `escapeForTitle`.

THEME CONTRACT / TOKENS / OVERLAY. `theme-contract-v1` is a CLOSED 24-token vocabulary: 15 COLOR_TOKENS, 7 DECORATION_TOKENS (3 radius + 3 shadow… actually 4 radius + 3 shadow), 2 TYPOGRAPHY_TOKENS. Typography is contract-representable but NEVER auto-applied (`generateThemeOverlay` skips `tokenKind === "typography"`; the theme gets a `typography-not-applied` compatibility warning) because a font swap changes line wrap and document height. The paint allowlist is closed at 11 properties: color, background-color, border-top/right/bottom/left, caret-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color (level 1) + border-radius, box-shadow (level 2); a non-themeable property reaching `declarationFor` is a THROWN `ThemeContractError`, not a warning. Three artifacts stay strictly apart: Theme File (site-agnostic, structurally cannot carry a selector/className/nodeId/route — token keys are the closed vocabulary and `isSafeThemeValue` refuses `;{}<>`, `url(`, `expression(`, `javascript:`, `@`, `\`, unbalanced quotes), Site Theme Adapter (the only artifact holding this site's `wr-st…` identities and `PaintGroup`s), and the generated Theme Overlay CSS. Border shorthands substitute ONLY the color component — `preservedPrefix` ("1px solid") is copied byte-for-byte, so the layout half is structurally untouchable. Overlay structure: `:root{--wr-theme-<token-dashed>:value;…}` then selector chunks of 25 reusing each paint group's selectors VERBATIM, winning by cascade order at identical specificity — no !important, no new class names.

THEME SERVE BOUNDARY, TWO FORMS. Preview: `startOverlayProxy` (theme/serve.ts) appends the overlay CSS to exactly ONE response — `/wr/generated-styles.css` — forcing `accept-encoding: identity` so the append is a plain concatenation. The served HTML is byte-identical with and without a theme, so hydration cannot be affected by construction, and with no theme there is no proxy at all. Production: the same ordering is reproduced statically by `bakeTheme` (a real file at `public/wr/theme-overlay.css`) plus `patchLayout` linking it after the generated sheet in the same `precedence="wr-generated"` group. Composition order across all layers is structural: Template → Content Overlay (server env / baked JSON) → Asset Rewrite → Theme Overlay (stylesheet append / link) → SEO Head Overlay (head splice) → Render. A theme run's manifest pins its `contentRunDir`, which is exactly why `STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.theme = ["template", "content"]` and why any content rerun stales the theme run too.

SLOT DOM IDENTITY — EVERY EMISSION SITE. `data-wr-node` is written into the runtime IR at three places in src/reconstruction/compile-node.ts: line 249 (`props["data-wr-node"] = node.nodeId` on every compiled element), lines 460-466 (inline SVG — the attribute is stamped onto the `<svg>` ROOT inside the opaque `v` markup via `annotateSvgRoot`, src/reconstruction/asset-resolver.ts:224; the wrapping host `<span class="wr-svg-host">` carries none), and lines 522-525 (`compileDocumentRoot`, where `<html>`/`<body>` become divs carrying `data-wr-node` + `data-wr-doc-tag`). `data-wr-dyn-node` is written at src/reconstruction/interaction-bindings.ts:850 (`props["data-wr-dyn-node"] = node.templateNodeId`) onto every node of a captured dynamic template; those props live serialized inside the trigger's `data-wr-obs` attribute and only reach the real DOM at client mount, in `buildTemplateNode` in src/reconstruction/runtime-template.ts (~lines 465-495, `createElement` + `setAttribute` per prop, never innerHTML). Everything else that mentions these attributes is a CSS selector consumer (pseudo-generator.ts:16, layout-inference.ts:471, qa-corrections.ts:190, interaction-bindings.ts:964/998-1000 reveal rules) or a QA/measurement reader (reconstruction-qa/capture-page.ts:298-314, capture-clone.ts:176, map-clone-nodes.ts, emit-diffs.ts:182/204, interaction-qa.ts:556/764; recon-template/parity-qa.ts:245-248,432,470,858,905; theme/theme-qa.ts:152,389,405; theme/occurrences.ts:117,125 which reads them off the IR rather than the DOM; content-injection/layout-qa.ts:170,324,405,495,510; production/qa.ts:729-733; release/brand-scan.ts:76). No code path adds a `data-wr-slot` attribute, and regions/types.ts:22-25 states that prohibition as policy.

SLOT-BINDINGS.JSON — WRITE AND READ SITES. Written exactly twice, both from the same in-memory `artifacts.bindingsFile` and never rewritten afterwards: src/recon-template/compile.ts:224 → `<template-run>/slot-bindings.json`, and src/recon-template/generate-template-app.ts:80 → `<template-run>/app/template-data/slot-bindings.json` (the runtime's copy). Read at: recon-template/validate-output.ts:120 (schema parse + cross-check that every `slot.bindingIds` matches, line 158), recon-template/parity-qa.ts:677, recon-template/app-templates.ts:113 (the generated app's `slot-content.ts`), content-injection/load-template.ts:64 (builds `bindingsBySlotId`), production/run.ts:406 (`pickContentProof`, filtered to surface=static / target=text / viewport=desktop), regions/load-input.ts:90 (plus `hashBytes` → `slotBindingsHash` recorded in the region artifact), and recon-template/report.ts:135 (in-memory). THE INVERSION lives in app-templates.ts `buildContract`: slotId→key via slots.json, each binding resolved against the (optionally overlaid) value, grouped into ops keyed `${pageId}|${viewport}`; `applySlotContent` then indexes the runtime tree by `node.n` (and dynamic-template nodes by `templateNodeId` inside the parsed `data-wr-obs` payload) and applies `text` / `attribute` / `svg-text` writes — every one guarded by `expectedValue`, with a `warnSkip` on mismatch. So slot→DOM identity is resolved on the IR before render; the rendered `data-wr-node` attribute is the JOIN KEY for QA and regions, never the write mechanism.
risks: AuthoredState has NO assets field (release/types.ts:221-229: only `slotValues`, `theme`, `updatedAt`). An asset replacement therefore cannot be authored the way slot values and theme tokens are — it survives only as an entry in `project.resolutions[]`, re-derived on every read via `effectiveResolution()`. `foldResolutionIntoAuthored` and `resolutionSlotValues` deliberately ignore `assets` and `fontDecisions`. A Visual Editor 'replace this image' write target does not exist yet; adding one means either extending AuthoredState (and the `assets` resolution slice in freshness.ts:resolutionSliceFor) or continuing to synthesize resolution packs.

`resolutionAssetContentHashes` hashes operator asset files BY PATH on every `refreshStageStatuses`. A file that is moved, deleted, or lives outside the repo becomes the sentinel `missing:<file>`, which permanently changes the assets inputsHash and re-stales assets + production on every command, with a warning. The bytes were already copied into the derived materialization run, so the rerun is unnecessary — but the freshness contract still points at the original path.

The assets stage runner does not re-measure. `applyAssetResolutions` INHERITS `report/network-qa.json` and `report/font-qa.json` from the base run (documented in report/derivation.json), so after providing a replacement image the residual census can still list that asset, and collect.ts:440-448 raises exactly that warning while a `runtime-source-asset-*` requirement may keep standing until an operator manually runs `pnpm assets:qa` against the new run. A stage that claims to close asset requirements cannot prove it closed them.

Any content-stage rerun cascades to four stages. `STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.theme = ["template","content"]` and seo likewise, so one authored slot value stales content → theme → seo → production. That is correct per the graph but means the cheapest possible authoring edit rebuilds and re-bakes the whole tail, including a real `next build`. Assets is the only stage genuinely orthogonal to content — and prepare.ts:334-337 already records the cost of that simplification as a project limitation (a content rerun does not re-run the asset inventory, so `replacement-manifest` slotKey joins can reference the earlier content run).

`CONTENT_DERIVED_HASH_EXCLUSIONS = ["report", "slot-accounting.json"]` and `slot-values.json` deliberately STAYS IN the content hash. Any NEW derived write into a content run directory that is not under `report/` will silently stale content plus every downstream stage. This exclusion set is recorded per-project in `ArtifactRef.excluded` and re-hashed from the RECORDED set, so a project prepared before a fix keeps the old semantics and only gets a `staleExclusionSetWarnings` warning — never a silent re-adoption.

`accounting.classify()` falls through to origin `user-provided` for any overlay value with no recorded `sources[key]`. The comment justifies it (only the §29 manual path can produce that), but it means a bug that drops provenance would report generated or invented copy as operator-supplied — the one origin value that also makes `applyTruthMode` treat a claim as backed. The release orchestrator's merge stamps `sources[key]="user-provided"` for every authored/routeContent/urls value, so authored content is immune to truth-mode refusal by construction while base-result values are not.

`verified-only` as the default is a real behaviour change relative to every Task 19-26 run, and truth-mode.ts documents it: re-ingesting an ARCHIVED generation result whose copy contains a percentage, a price or 'trusted by' phrasing now DEMOTES that value from `slotValues` to `unresolved`. Any release rerun that re-ingests a historical base result can therefore move a project from PRODUCTION_READY to INPUTS_REQUIRED. The escape hatch (`--truth-mode synthetic-allowed`) is lossless but must be chosen explicitly.

`buildPreviewBlockers` is a hardcoded 7-entry list whose PROSE is fixed even though its numbers are derived per site. Only `uninjected-route-content` has a suppression rule (dropped at 0). The other six are emitted unconditionally in preview mode — e.g. `fonts-license-needs-review` prints 'no font is self-hosted' even where an operator has recorded `self-host-license-verified` font decisions in the derived materialization run, because run.ts reads `fontInventory.license` and never consults `font-decisions.json`.

production/patch.ts is a four-anchor tripwire over generated app source (`next.config.mjs`, `app/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`, `src/runtime/slot-content.ts`, `app/layout.tsx`). Any change to `SLOT_CONTENT_TS`, `NODE_RENDERER_TSX`, the layout template or the page template in src/recon-template/app-templates.ts or src/reconstruction/app-template.ts will break the production bake with a loud 'patch anchor not found' — which is the designed behaviour, but it makes those templates a shared frozen surface between the template compiler and the production compiler.

There is no per-route authored SEO title seam. `buildProductionSeoPlan` derives every injected route's title as the literal `${workingName} | ${category}` and its description as `${pagePlan.primaryMessage} — ${positioning}`; uninjected routes get a brand-only `previewFallback`. `routeContent[route].pagePlan.primaryMessage` is the only operator lever, and it only moves the description. Authoring a real per-route title today requires changing production-plan.ts, not supplying data.

`brand-surfaces.ts` names 14 surfaces including `svg-aria-label` and `svg-symbol-id`, which live in the runtime IR's opaque `v` markup and have NO slot binding — so there is no write target and no neutralization anywhere in the pipeline. The module's own header states neutralization belongs at BAKE and is sequenced after Content V2 / region enablement. Consequently the `source-brand-asset` requirement (release-blocking severity) can be raised but cannot be resolved by any code path that exists today.

`RegionPlanFile.unassignedUnitIds` is expected to be non-empty and is documented as honest rather than defective — PageRegion granularity follows the markup, and a template with little sectioning markup yields few regions. Any future logic that treats region coverage as a completeness metric would be reading that number wrong. Note also that content-injection reaches PageRegion only through the narrow duck-typed `PageRegionsContractSchema` in region-plan.ts and never imports src/regions, so an id-moving policy change over there is invisible here except as different region ids.
